metadata.description: GitHub Actions workflow deploying to Azure, triggered by push and workflow_dispatch events.

extras.workflow_content:
name: Deploy to Azure

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-backend
  AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH: './python-backend'
  PYTHON_VERSION: '3.11'
  NODE_VERSION: '20'
  RESOURCE_GROUP: openai-cs-agents-demo-rg
  LOCATION: eastus2
  APP_SERVICE_PLAN: openai-cs-agents-plan
  STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-frontend

jobs:
  build-and-deploy-backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./python-backend
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Resource Group (if not exists)
        run: |
          az group create --name ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} || true

      - name: Create App Service Plan (Free Tier)
        run: |
          az appservice plan create \
            --name ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --sku F1 \
            --is-linux || true

      - name: Create Web App
        run: |
          az webapp create \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --plan ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --runtime "PYTHON:3.11" || true

      - name: Configure App Settings
        run: |
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings \
              OPENAI_API_KEY="${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}" \
              SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT=true \
              WEBSITES_PORT=8000

      - name: Configure startup command
        run: |
          az webapp config set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --startup-file "gunicorn -w 2 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker api:app --bind 0.0.0.0:8000"

      - name: Deploy to Azure Web App
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}
          package: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH }}

      - name: Output Backend URL
        id: backend-url
        run: |
          BACKEND_URL="https://${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}.azurewebsites.net"
          echo "BACKEND_URL=$BACKEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Backend deployed to: $BACKEND_URL"

    outputs:
      backend_url: ${{ steps.backend-url.outputs.BACKEND_URL }}

  build-and-deploy-frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build-and-deploy-backend
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}

      - name: Install pnpm
        run: npm install -g pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm run build
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Static Web App (if not exists)
        run: |
          az staticwebapp create \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} \
            --sku Free || true

      - name: Get Static Web App deployment token
        id: swa-token
        run: |
          TOKEN=$(az staticwebapp secrets list \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "properties.apiKey" -o tsv)
          echo "::add-mask::$TOKEN"
          echo "DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN=$TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Deploy to Azure Static Web Apps
        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1
        with:
          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ steps.swa-token.outputs.DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN }}
          repo_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          action: "upload"
          app_location: "./ui/out"
          output_location: ""
          skip_app_build: true

      - name: Output Frontend URL
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "Frontend deployed to: https://$FRONTEND_URL"

  configure-cors:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-and-deploy-backend, build-and-deploy-frontend]
    
    steps:
      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Get Static Web App URL
        id: frontend-url
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "FRONTEND_URL=https://$FRONTEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Configure CORS on Backend
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL="${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"
          # Pass ALLOWED_ORIGINS to FastAPI's CORSMiddleware via app setting.
          # Do NOT use `az webapp cors add` together with FastAPI's own CORSMiddleware —
          # both would add Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers, causing duplicate-header
          # rejections in browsers.  FastAPI's middleware is the single source of truth.
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings ALLOWED_ORIGINS="$FRONTEND_URL,http://localhost:3250,http://localhost:3000"
          # Clear any previously-added Azure-level CORS origins to avoid conflicts.
          az webapp cors remove \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --allowed-origins "*" || true

      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "=== Deployment Complete ==="
          echo "Backend URL: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}"
          echo "Frontend URL: ${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"

summary.use_case: This text-only AI system uses an agentic workflow with specialized agents for FAQ answering, request triage, and routing, serving customer support needs. It features five GPT-4-mini agents (Cancellation, FAQ, Flight Status, Seat Booking, Triage) with two guardrails (jailbreak and relevance) deployed via Azure with SQLite storage. The system does not support voice, image, or video modalities.
summary.iac_security_summary:
## Security briefing

### 1) Deployment posture
- **Cloud provider / runtime:** Azure (from `az webapp` and `Azure Credentials` IAM node); application servers Gunicorn and Uvicorn detected.
- **Regions / HA / resilience:** Not evidenced.
- **Assessment:** The deployment uses Azure App Service with Gunicorn/Uvicorn application servers, but no high-availability or multi-region configuration is evidenced.

### 2) Secret management
- **Secret stores:** `github_actions_secret` (from `secret_store` field in "Deploy to Azure" node).
- **Credential handling:** Azure credentials are provided via `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}` — a GitHub Actions secret reference, not a plaintext secret.
- **Assessment:** Credentials are stored in GitHub Actions secrets, but the use of long-lived Azure secrets rather than short-lived OIDC tokens increases credential exposure risk.

### 3) Encryption
- **Encryption at rest:** `encryption_at_rest_coverage` is `false`.
- **Key management:** Not evidenced.
- **Assessment:** Encryption at rest is not configured for the infrastructure, and no key management details are present.

### 4) IAM / least privilege
- **Principals / service accounts:** `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}` is the sole IAM principal.
- **Scope / permissions / trust:** Principal has subscription-level scope (`iam_scope: "subscription"`) and trusts `github-actions` principals, but exact permissions are not evidenced.
- **Assessment:** The subscription-wide scope is overly broad and violates least-privilege principles.

### 5) CI/CD security
- **Runners / triggers:** GitHub Actions runners (`ubuntu-latest`); triggers include `push` and `workflow_dispatch`.
- **OIDC / credential flow:** OIDC is not used (`uses_oidc: false`); credentials are injected via GitHub Actions secrets.
- **Assessment:** Without OIDC, long-lived Azure secrets are passed to runners, increasing the risk of credential leakage.

### 6) Container security
- **Images / root user:** Not evidenced.
- **Health checks / resource limits:** Not evidenced.
- **Assessment:** No container configuration details are available in the provided data.

### 7) Top 3 prioritized actions
1. **Enable OIDC for GitHub Actions** – Replace long-lived `AZURE_CREDENTIALS` with OIDC-based federated identity to eliminate secret injection into CI/CD workflows.
2. **Scope IAM permissions** – Reduce the Azure credential scope from `subscription` to a resource group or specific resources to enforce least privilege.
3. **Enable encryption at rest** – Configure Azure Storage Service Encryption or customer-managed keys for all data stores associated with the deployment.

relationship_graph_md:
## Component Relationship Graph

- **Architecture Overview**: The system uses a FastAPI framework with Bearer Auth-protected endpoints (Login, Me, Logout, Chat). A `Chat Endpoint` feeds into `OpenAI Agents` which delegates to a `Triage Agent`, then to specialized agents (`Flight Status`, `FAQ`, `Cancellation`, `Seat Booking`). All agents use the `gpt-4.1-mini` model and call shared tools (Baggage, Cancel Flight, Display Seat Map, Faq Lookup, Flight Status).

- **Data Flow**: User requests hit authenticated endpoints → Triage Agent delegates to domain agents → agents invoke tools (e.g., `Cancel Flight`) and call the model for responses. `Relevance` and `Jailbreak` guardrails filter model outputs only; they do not gate tool calls or agent-to-tool access.

- **Security Observations**:  
  - **No guardrails on tool execution**: Agents can call all tools (`Cancel Flight`, `Update Seat`, etc.) without any guardrail checks before or after invocation.  
  - **Unguarded datastores**: `Sqlite` is listed but has no connections shown—implies data may be accessible via tools without oversight.  
  - **External model call**: All agents use `gpt-4.1-mini` directly; no guardrail on model input (only output checked).  
  - **Overprivileged agents**: All agents (including `FAQ Agent`) can call destructive tools like `Cancel Flight`—no least-privilege separation.  
  - **Missing guardrail on `Jailbreak Guardrail Instructions`**: This prompt has no data flow connections, suggesting it may be unused or misconfigured.
